Behind the Bell Assistant

Episode-prep help for STA's K-12 education podcast.

What it is

A shared Claude.ai Project for the three hosts of Behind the Bell - Jessie Christensen, Adam Baker, and Pat McInerny - that helps any host plan and prepare an episode from start to finish. Name a topic and a guest, and it returns a full prep package with sourced, fact-checked content.

What it does

  • Answers questions about a guest or topic and brainstorms episode angles.
  • Produces guest research and full prep packages (HTML, or Word on request).
  • Writes grouped interview questions and a loose run-of-show script.
  • Drafts guest-outreach emails for the host to review and send.

How to access it

  1. Log in at claude.ai with your School Technology work email.
  2. Open Behind the Bell Assistant from your Projects list (it is shared with the three hosts).
  3. Start a new conversation and tell it the episode topic and guest - it will ask for anything else it needs.
"We're having Dr. Lena Ruiz on to talk about chronic absenteeism. Build me a prep package - guest background, three question groups, and a draft outreach email."

How it keeps facts honest

Because hosts read these facts on published episodes, every claim is tagged [CONFIRMED] or [UNVERIFIED] with its source, so nothing unverified slips on air. If it cannot confirm a fact, it says so rather than guessing.

Not a sales pitch. Behind the Bell is an educator-to-educator conversation, not a platform to promote STA or Skyward. The assistant flags and rewrites anything that drifts toward a pitch.

Good to know

  • It is a Claude.ai Project, so it works from its uploaded context (the show profile, prep and script formats, guest list, and email templates) - it does not browse the live web or your calendar.
  • Prep packages come as formatted HTML by default; ask for a Word version when you want an editable doc.
  • Questions about timing, the show roadmap, or new features go to Adam.
